To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the selectivity filters of TRPV5 channels are rapidly accessible to positively and negatively charged methanethiosulfonate derivatives and that the accessibility of residues in the filter is dependent on the presence of specific amino acids in the filter.

(i) The selectivity filter in the TRPV5 Ca(2+) channel is highly accessible from the external surface; (ii) The accessibility of the selectivity pore in the TRPV Ca(2+) channels is dependent on the number of carboxylates at position 542; and (iii) The selectivity of the TRPV Ca2+ channels is dependent on carboxylates in the selectivity pore.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of TRP channels, in particular the TRPV5 calcium channel.
the molecular basis of the selectivity for Ca(2+) in TRPV5.
understanding the structural basis for ion selectivity of the TRPV channel family, with particular emphasis on the role of the selectivity filters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selectivity of the TRPV channel to Ca(2+) is determined by a combination of the size and charge of the amino acid side chains at positions 541, 543, and 547 in the selectivity pore.
the side chains in the selectivity of the TRPV channel are rapidly accessible from both the extracellular side and the intracellular side.
the selectivity filters of TRPV5 and K(+) channels are structurally different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selectivity filters of the TRPV channel and K(+) channel are structurally distinct.
the selectivity of the TRPV channel to Ca(2+) may be determined by a combination of electrostatic and steric factors.
the TRPV5 selectivity filter is a flexible structure that can adopt a constricted state when the carboxylates of D542 are present and an open structure when the D542 carboxylates are absent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCAM can be used to map the topology of the TRPV channel pore.

the selectivity of the TRPV channel is not determined by the presence of carboxylate side chains at the constriction site of the selectivity pore but is instead a consequence of the overall structure of the select channel.

the selectivity filters of TRPV5 and other TRP channels are more accessible to external reagents than the selectivity filters in K(+) and Na(+) channels, suggesting that they may be more permeable to external reagents and other ions.
